questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match reactions in Column I with the corresponding products formed as given in Column II.
Column IColumn II
A. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\ \text{Cl}^- + \dfrac{\text{H}_2\text{O}}{warm} \rightarrow$P. p–Bromophenol
B. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \dfrac{\text{Br}_2\ \text{in}\ \text{CS}_2}{273K} \rightarrow$Q. 2,4,6–Tribromophenol
C. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \dfrac{(i)\ \text{CHCl}_3 + \text{NaOH}(aq)}{(ii)\ \text{HCl}} \rightarrow$R. Phenol
D. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{Br}_2\ (aq) \rightarrow$S. 2–Hydroxybenzaldehyde
options: A - S B - R C - Q D - P
A - R B - P C - S D - Q
A - Q B - R C - S D - P
A - Q B - P C - S D - R
questions.solution:
Reaction A: Warming benzene diazonium chloride with water yields phenol. Thus, A matches with R.

Reaction B: Bromination of phenol in a non-polar solvent like $CS_2$ at low temperature ($273$ K) yields monobromophenols, primarily p-bromophenol as the major product. Thus, B matches with P.

Reaction C: Phenol reacts with chloroform in the presence of aqueous $NaOH$ followed by acidification to form 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde). This is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction. Thus, C matches with S.

Reaction D: Phenol reacts with bromine water to form a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol. Thus, D matches with Q.

The correct matching is A - R, B - P, C - S, D - Q.

Answer: A - R B - P C - S D - Q

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aliphatic compound [X], Molecular formula ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) can be prepared from Acetone and R– Mg–X. [X] with 20% Phosphoric acid gives an unsaturated compound $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$ [Y]. Compound [Y] is also obtained on heating [X] with Copper metal at 573K. [X] shows no reaction with PCC but on heating with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ it forms Acetone + $\text{CO}_2$ + $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Compounds [X] and [Y] are -------------------- and --------------------
questions.solution:
Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) reacts with methylmagnesium halide ($\text{CH}_3\text{MgX}$) followed by hydrolysis to form a tertiary alcohol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgX} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH}$

Thus, compound [X] is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, which has the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

Dehydration of [X] with 20% $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ or heating with Cu at 573 K yields 2-methylpropene [Y].

$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Tertiary alcohols do not undergo oxidation with PCC, hence [X] shows no reaction.

Vigorous oxidation of [X] with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ involves dehydration to [Y] followed by oxidative cleavage of the double bond to form acetone, $\text{CO}_2$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Therefore, [X] is 2-methylpropan-2-ol and [Y] is 2-methylpropene.

Answer: [X]: 2–Methylpropan–2–ol [Y]: 2–Methylpropene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: Anisole is prepared by reaction between Bromobenzene and Sodium methoxide
Tert. butyl methyl ether reacts with Conc. HI on heating to form 2–Iodo–2–methylpropane and Methanol by $S_N1$ mechanism
Isopropyl methyl ether reacts with Conc. HI to produce isopropyl alcohol and methyl iodide by $S_N2$ mechanism
Anisole reacts with Ethanoyl chloride / anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ in $\text{CS}_2$ to form 4–Methoxyacetophenone in larger amount
questions.solution:
Bromobenzene does not undergo nucleophilic substitution easily due to the partial double bond character of the C-Br bond. Therefore, anisole cannot be prepared by the reaction between bromobenzene and sodium methoxide.

Anisole is prepared by Williamson ether synthesis using sodium phenoxide and methyl halide (such as methyl bromide or methyl iodide).

Tert-butyl methyl ether reacts with concentrated HI via an $S_N1$ mechanism because the tert-butyl carbocation is highly stable, yielding 2-iodo-2-methylpropane and methanol.

Isopropyl methyl ether reacts with concentrated HI via an $S_N2$ mechanism where the iodide ion attacks the less sterically hindered methyl group, producing methyl iodide and isopropyl alcohol.

Anisole undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with ethanoyl chloride and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form 4-methoxyacetophenone as the major product due to the para-directing nature of the methoxy group and less steric hindrance at the para position.

Thus, the statement in option (A) is wrong.

Answer: Anisole is prepared by reaction between Bromobenzene and Sodium methoxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes?
options: The hydrogensulphite addition product is useful for separation and purification of aldehydes
Aldehydes and ketones react very slowly with pure HCN to yield cyanohydrins
2,4 DNP derivatives are useful to identify aldehydes and ketones
questions.solution:
Hemiacetals contain one alkoxy group ($-OR$) and one hydroxyl group ($-OH$) attached to the same carbon atom. They are gem-alkoxyalcohols. Acetals contain two alkoxy groups attached to the same carbon atom and are known as gem-dialkoxy compounds. Thus, the statement that hemiacetals are gem-dialkoxy compounds is incorrect.

The sodium bisulphite addition product is crystalline and water-soluble, and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound by treating it with dilute mineral acid or alkali. Therefore, it is useful for the separation and purification of aldehydes.

Pure $HCN$ reacts very slowly with aldehydes and ketones because it is a weak acid and generates cyanide ions very slowly. The reaction is typically catalyzed by a base.

2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine reacts with aldehydes and ketones to form 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazones, which are usually yellow, orange, or red solids, making them useful for characterization.

Answer: Hemiacetals are gem-dialkoxy compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Propanal on reaction with dilute NaOH, undergoes aldol condensation resulting in the formation of a compound A. Identify the correct structure of A and name of the compound.
questions.solution:
Propanal ($CH_3-CH_2-CHO$) undergoes self-aldol condensation in the presence of dilute NaOH.

The $\alpha$-carbon of one propanal molecule is deprotonated by the base to form an enolate ion:
$CH_3-CH_2-CHO + OH^- \rightleftharpoons CH_3-\bar{C}H-CHO + H_2O$

This enolate ion acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of a second propanal molecule:
$CH_3-CH_2-CHO + CH_3-\bar{C}H-CHO \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH(O^-)-CH(CH_3)-CHO$

Protonation of the resulting alkoxide ion from water yields the aldol product (Compound A):
$CH_3-CH_2-CH(O^-)-CH(CH_3)-CHO + H_2O \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH(CH_3)-CHO + OH^-$

To name this compound according to IUPAC rules, we select the longest carbon chain containing the aldehyde group, which has 5 carbon atoms (pentanal). Numbering starts from the aldehyde carbon:
C1: $-CHO$
C2: $-CH(CH_3)-$
C3: $-CH(OH)-$
C4: $-CH_2-$
C5: $-CH_3$

There is a methyl group at C2 and a hydroxy group at C3. Thus, the IUPAC name is 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal. This matches the structure and name given in option (D).

Answer: 3-hydroxy-2-methyl-pentanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Etard reaction is a method of preparation of benzaldehyde by oxidation of toluene. The oxidizing agent used in this reaction is:
questions.solution:
The Etard reaction involves the oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde.

The oxidizing agent used in this reaction is chromyl chloride ($CrO_2Cl_2$) dissolved in a non-polar solvent such as $CS_2$ or $CCl_4$.

The reaction proceeds via the formation of a brown chromium complex, which upon hydrolysis yields benzaldehyde.

Answer: Chromyl chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reagent used in carbylamine reaction is ----------------------- and the product of the reaction will be ---------------
questions.solution:
The carbylamine reaction is a characteristic test for primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic).

When a primary amine is heated with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($\text{KOH}$), it forms an isocyanide (also known as carbylamine), which has a characteristic foul smell.

The general reaction is:
$R-\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH (alc.)} \xrightarrow{\Delta} R-\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, the reagent used is alcoholic $\text{KOH} + \text{CHCl}_3$ and the product is an isocyanide.

Answer: Alcoholic $\text{KOH} + \text{CHCl}_3$ ; isocyanide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct reaction of Hinsberg's reagent with primary, secondary and tertiary amines?
options: Tertiary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is insoluble in alkali
Primary amine forms N-alkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
Secondary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
Primary amine forms N, N-dialkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali
questions.solution:
Hinsberg's reagent is benzenesulphonyl chloride ($C_6H_5SO_2Cl$).

Primary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to form N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide. The hydrogen attached to the nitrogen in the sulphonamide is strongly acidic due to the presence of the strong electron-withdrawing sulphonyl group. Hence, it is soluble in alkali.

Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide. Since N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and hence insoluble in alkali.

Tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form sulphonamides.

Therefore, primary amine forms N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide which is soluble in alkali.

Answer: Primary amine forms N-alkyl Benzene sulphonamide which is soluble in alkali

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct order of the type of reactions taking place in this sequence:
questions.solution:
Nitrobenzene is converted to Aniline using $Sn/HCl$. This involves the removal of oxygen and addition of hydrogen, which is a Reduction reaction.

Aniline reacts with $NaNO_2/HCl$ (which forms $HNO_2$ in situ) to form Benzene Diazonium Chloride. The process of conversion of a primary aromatic amine into its diazonium salt is called Diazotization.

Benzene Diazonium Chloride reacts with another molecule of aniline in a mildly acidic medium to form $p$-amino Azobenzene. This is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the diazonium ion acts as an electrophile. This specific type of reaction forming an azo dye is known as a Coupling reaction.

Therefore, the correct sequence of reactions is Reduction, Diazotization, Coupling.

Answer: Reduction, Diazotization, Coupling

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of structural isomers possible for a compound with molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ is:
questions.solution:
Degree of unsaturation for $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ is $3 - \dfrac{9}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = 0$.

The compound is a saturated aliphatic amine. It can exist as primary, secondary, or tertiary amines.

Primary amines ($1^{\circ}$):
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (Propan-1-amine)
2. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (Propan-2-amine)

Secondary amines ($2^{\circ}$):
3. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$ (N-Methylethanamine)

Tertiary amines ($3^{\circ}$):
4. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ (N,N-Dimethylmethanamine)

Total number of structural isomers is $4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the name of the reaction involved in conversion of A→B and name the compound B.
\(\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CN} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}]{\mathrm{H}^{+}} \mathrm{A} \cdot \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}^{+} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}]{\mathrm{Cl} 2 / \text { Red Phosphorous }} \mathrm{B}\)
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of methyl cyanide in the presence of an acid yields ethanoic acid.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CN} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H}^+ / \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH}$ (Compound A)

Ethanoic acid reacts with chlorine in the presence of red phosphorus to give $\alpha$-chloroethanoic acid. This reaction is known as the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COOH} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H}^+ / \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]{\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \text{Red P}} \mathrm{ClCH}_2\mathrm{COOH}$ (Compound B)

Compound B is 2-chloroethanoic acid.

Answer: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, 2-chloro-ethanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The secondary structure of protein consists of:
options: A folding of the polypeptide chains which exists as fibrous and globular
Two or more polypeptide chains which exist as sub-units
A long polypeptide chain which exists $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structure
A long chain of amino acids linked with each other in a specific sequence
questions.solution:
The primary structure of a protein refers to the specific sequence of amino acids in the polypeptide chain.

The secondary structure refers to the local folded structures that form within a polypeptide due to hydrogen bonding between the backbone amide and carbonyl groups. The most common types of secondary structures are the $\alpha$-helix and the $\beta$-pleated sheet.

The tertiary structure refers to the overall three-dimensional folding of the entire polypeptide chain, which gives rise to fibrous and globular shapes.

The quaternary structure refers to the arrangement of multiple polypeptide chains (sub-units) into a single functional protein complex.

Therefore, the secondary structure consists of a long polypeptide chain which exists as an $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structure.

Answer: A long polypeptide chain which exists $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is an INCORRECT statement?
options: Polysaccharides are known as non-sugars as they are not sweet in taste
In monosaccharides, aldoses are reducing sugars while ketoses are non-reducing sugars
In D (+) Glucose, D represents the configuration similar to D-Glyceraldehyde
D (-) fructose forms a five membered ring known as furanose which is in analogy with the compound furan
questions.solution:
All monosaccharides, whether aldoses or ketoses, are reducing sugars. Ketoses such as fructose can reduce Tollens' and Fehling's reagents because they undergo isomerization to aldoses in the alkaline medium via an enediol intermediate. Thus, the statement that ketoses are non-reducing sugars is incorrect.

Polysaccharides are indeed called non-sugars because they are not sweet in taste.

The 'D' in D-(+)-Glucose indicates that the configuration at the highest numbered chiral carbon is the same as that of D-Glyceraldehyde.

D-(-)-Fructose exists as a five-membered cyclic structure called furanose, which is named by analogy to the heterocyclic compound furan.

Answer: In monosaccharides, aldoses are reducing sugars while ketoses are non-reducing sugars

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct match?
questions.solution:
DNA contains $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose sugar, whereas RNA contains $\beta$-D-ribose sugar.

RNA molecules (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) are directly responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.

Glucocorticoids are steroid hormones secreted by the adrenal cortex that regulate carbohydrate metabolism and stress responses, not hyperthyroidism.

Deficiency of Vitamin A causes night blindness and xerophthalmia, whereas deficiency of Vitamin B6 causes convulsions.

Therefore, the only correct match is RNA - Protein Synthesis.

Answer: RNA - Protein Synthesis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The hybridisation of atomic orbitals of nitrogen in $\text{NO}_2^+$, $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{NH}_4^+$ are respectively
questions.solution:
For $\text{NO}_2^+$: The central nitrogen atom has $5 - 1 = 4$ valence electrons. It forms two double bonds with two oxygen atoms. The number of $\sigma$ bonds is $2$ and there are no lone pairs. Steric number $= 2$. Hybridisation is $sp$.

For $\text{NO}_3^-$: The central nitrogen atom forms three $\sigma$ bonds with three oxygen atoms and has no lone pairs. Steric number $= 3$. Hybridisation is $sp^2$.

For $\text{NH}_4^+$: The central nitrogen atom has $5 - 1 = 4$ valence electrons. It forms four $\sigma$ bonds with four hydrogen atoms and has no lone pairs. Steric number $= 4$. Hybridisation is $sp^3$.

The hybridisations are $sp$, $sp^2$, and $sp^3$ respectively.

Answer: $sp, sp^2,\ sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following options represent the correct bond order?
questions.solution:
The number of electrons in O_2$ is 16.

The electronic configuration of O_2$ is $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{*1} \pi_{2p_y}^{*1}$.

Bond order of O_2 = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a) = \frac{1}{2}(10 - 6) = 2.0$.

The number of electrons in O_2^{+}$ is 15. One electron is removed from the antibonding $\pi_{2p}^{*}$ orbital.

Bond order of O_2^{+} = \frac{1}{2}(10 - 5) = 2.5$.

The number of electrons in O_2^{-}$ is 17. One electron is added to the antibonding $\pi_{2p}^{*}$ orbital.

Bond order of O_2^{-} = \frac{1}{2}(10 - 7) = 1.5$.

Thus, the correct order of bond order is O_2^{-} \lt  \text{O}_2 \lt  \text{O}_2^{+}$.

Answer: O_2^- < \text{O}_2 < \text{O}_2^+

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The highest dipole moment is for:
questions.solution:
The molecules $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{CCl}_4$ have highly symmetrical tetrahedral geometries, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

For $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{CHCl}_3$, the net dipole moment is the vector sum of the individual C-H and C-Cl bond dipoles. In $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$, the resultant of the two C-Cl bond dipoles and the two C-H bond dipoles reinforce each other more effectively than the bond dipoles in $\text{CHCl}_3$.

The experimental dipole moments are:
$\text{CH}_4 = 0 \text{ D}$
$\text{CCl}_4 = 0 \text{ D}$
$\text{CHCl}_3 = 1.04 \text{ D}$
$\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 = 1.60 \text{ D}$

Thus, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ has the highest dipole moment among the given options.

Answer: $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the gaseous equilibrium
$2\text{AB}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{AB}_{(g)} + \text{B}_{2(g)}$
The expression relating the degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) and equilibrium constant ($K_p$) and total pressure P is:
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $2\text{AB}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{AB}_{(g)} + \text{B}_{2(g)}$

Let the initial moles of $\text{AB}_2$ be $2$.

Moles at equilibrium:
$\text{AB}_2 = 2(1-\alpha)$
$\text{AB} = 2\alpha$
$\text{B}_2 = \alpha$

Total moles at equilibrium $= 2(1-\alpha) + 2\alpha + \alpha = 2 + \alpha$

Partial pressures at equilibrium:
$P_{\text{AB}_2} = \dfrac{2(1-\alpha)}{2+\alpha}P$
$P_{\text{AB}} = \dfrac{2\alpha}{2+\alpha}P$
$P_{\text{B}_2} = \dfrac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}P$

The equilibrium constant $K_p$ is given by:
$K_p = \dfrac{(P_{\text{AB}})^2 P_{\text{B}_2}}{(P_{\text{AB}_2})^2}$

Substituting the partial pressures:
$K_p = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2\alpha}{2+\alpha}P\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2+\alpha}P\right)}{\left(\dfrac{2(1-\alpha)}{2+\alpha}P\right)^2}$

$K_p = \dfrac{4\alpha^2 P^2}{(2+\alpha)^2} \times \dfrac{\alpha P}{2+\alpha} \times \dfrac{(2+\alpha)^2}{4(1-\alpha)^2 P^2}$

$K_p = \dfrac{\alpha^3 P}{(2+\alpha)(1-\alpha)^2}$

Assuming $\alpha$ is very small ($\alpha \ll 1$), we can approximate $2+\alpha \approx 2$ and $1-\alpha \approx 1$.

$K_p = \dfrac{\alpha^3 P}{2}$

$\alpha^3 = \dfrac{2K_p}{P}$

$\alpha = \left(\dfrac{2K_p}{P}\right)^{1/3}$

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{2K_p}{P}\right)^{1/3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
If the equilibrium constant for $\text{N}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_{(g)}$ is 49
The equilibrium constant for the reaction $\text{NO}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \dfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2(g)}$ is __________
questions.solution:
For the given reaction $\text{N}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_{(g)}$, the equilibrium constant is $K_1 = 49$.

The required reaction is $\text{NO}_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \dfrac{1}{2}\text{N}_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2(g)}$.

This reaction is obtained by reversing the given reaction and multiplying the stoichiometric coefficients by $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

The new equilibrium constant $K_2$ is related to $K_1$ as:

$K_2 = (K_1)^{-\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K_1}}$

Substituting the value of $K_1$:

$K_2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{49}} = \dfrac{1}{7} \approx 0.143$

Answer: $0.143$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The rate constants for two different reactions, $k_1$ and $k_2$ are $10^{16}\cdot e^{-2000/T}$ and $10^{15}\cdot e^{-1000/T}$ respectively. The temperature at which $k_1 = k_2$ is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
60% of a first order reaction was completed in 60 min, then 50% of the same reaction can be completed in:
[log 4 = 0.60, log 5=0.69]
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a-x} \right)$

Given that $60\%$ of the reaction is completed in $60$ minutes:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{60} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{100-60} \right)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{60} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{40} \right) = \dfrac{2.303}{60} \log (2.5)$

Using the given values, $\log (2.5) = \log \left( \dfrac{10}{4} \right) = \log 10 - \log 4 = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{60} \times 0.40$

The time required for $50\%$ completion (half-life) is:

$t_{50\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{100}{100-50} \right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log 2$

Since $\log 4 = 0.60$, we have $2 \log 2 = 0.60 \Rightarrow \log 2 = 0.30$

Substituting the value of $k$:

$t_{50\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{\dfrac{2.303}{60} \times 0.40} \times 0.30$

$t_{50\%} = 60 \times \dfrac{0.30}{0.40} = 60 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 45\ \text{min}$

Answer: $45\ \text{min}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct values to be plotted in the graph, the slope of which can be used to determine the activation energy of a reaction.
questions.solution:
According to the Arrhenius equation:

$k = A e^{-E_a / RT}$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides:

$\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{RT}$

This equation represents a straight line of the form $y = mx + c$, where $y = \ln k$ and $x = \dfrac{1}{T}$.

Plotting $\ln k$ versus $\dfrac{1}{T}$ yields a straight line with slope $m = -\dfrac{E_a}{R}$.

Thus, the activation energy $E_a$ can be determined from the slope of this graph.

Answer: $\ln k\ vs\ \dfrac{1}{T}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rate law can be determined from a balanced chemical equation if
options: one of the reactants is in excess
there is a sequence of elementary reactions
questions.solution:
For an elementary reaction, the reaction occurs in a single step. The molecularity of an elementary reaction is equal to its overall order. Therefore, the rate law can be written directly from the stoichiometric coefficients of the reactants in the balanced chemical equation.

Answer: it is an elementary reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When the initial concentration of a zero order reaction is doubled, the half-life of the reaction is:
questions.solution:
For a zero order reaction, the half-life is given by the expression:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$

where $[A]_0$ is the initial concentration and $k$ is the rate constant.

This shows that the half-life is directly proportional to the initial concentration ($t_{1/2} \propto [A]_0$).

Therefore, when the initial concentration is doubled, the half-life of the reaction is also doubled.

Answer: doubled

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the Coordination compounds in Column I with the type of stereoisomerism given in Column II exhibited by them.
Column IColumn II
A. $[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$P. fac-mer
B. $\text{Ni}[(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$Q. cis-trans
C. $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$R. only cis isomer shows optical isomerism
D. $[\text{Pt}\,\text{Cl}_2(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$S. does not exhibit isomerism.
options: A - Q B - S C - P D - R
A - R B - P C - S D - Q
A - S B - P C - Q D - R
A - S B - R C - Q D - P
questions.solution:
$[\text{Pt}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $MA_2B_2$. It exhibits cis-trans isomerism. This matches Q.

$[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_2\text{Cl}_2]$ is a tetrahedral complex of the type $MA_2B_2$ since $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is a $3d^8$ ion and forms $sp^3$ hybridized complexes with weak field ligands. Tetrahedral complexes do not exhibit geometrical isomerism, and since it lacks four different ligands, it does not show optical isomerism. Thus, it does not exhibit isomerism. This matches S.

$[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_3B_3$. It exhibits facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomerism. This matches P.

$[\text{PtCl}_2(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $M(AA)_2B_2$. It exhibits cis-trans isomerism. The cis isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active, while the trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. This matches R.

Therefore, A matches Q, B matches S, C matches P, and D matches R.

Answer: A - Q B - S C - P D - R

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Crystal Field Stabilisation energy of (i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$ and (ii) $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$ are ----- and ------- respectively.
questions.solution:
For the complex $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$:
The oxidation state of Co is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $3d^6$.
Since $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The electrons are distributed in the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals as $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times n_{t_{2g}} + 0.6 \times n_{e_g}) \Delta_0$
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 4 + 0.6 \times 2) \Delta_0 = (-1.6 + 1.2) \Delta_0 = -0.4 \Delta_0$

For the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}$:
The oxidation state of Fe is $+3$. The electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is $3d^5$.
Since $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand, the complex is high-spin. The electrons are distributed as $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$.
$\text{CFSE} = (-0.4 \times 3 + 0.6 \times 2) \Delta_0 = (-1.2 + 1.2) \Delta_0 = 0 \Delta_0$

Answer: (i) $-0.4\Delta_0$ (ii) $0\ \Delta_0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ion that has a spin only magnetic moment of 5.9 BM is:
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.9$ BM, we have $\sqrt{n(n+2)} = 5.9$. Squaring both sides gives $n(n+2) \approx 35$, which corresponds to $n = 5$ unpaired electrons.

Let us determine the number of unpaired electrons for each given ion:

For $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ (Atomic number of Fe = 26):
Electronic configuration of Fe is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 4s^2$.
Electronic configuration of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 5$.

For $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ (Atomic number of Ni = 28):
Electronic configuration of Ni is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.
Electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 2$.

For $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ (Atomic number of Mn = 25):
Electronic configuration of Mn is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^2$.
Electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 4$.

For $\text{Co}^{3+}$ (Atomic number of Co = 27):
Electronic configuration of Co is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^7 4s^2$.
Electronic configuration of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 4$ (or $0$ in low spin complexes).

Since $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ has $5$ unpaired electrons, its spin-only magnetic moment is $\sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.

Answer: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following species will impart colour to an aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
The colour of transition metal ions in aqueous solution is due to d-d transitions, which require the presence of unpaired d-electrons (partially filled d-subshell).

The electronic configurations of the given ions are:
$\text{Cr}^{3+}$ (Z = 24): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^3$ (3 unpaired electrons)
$\text{Cu}^+$ (Z = 29): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}$ (0 unpaired electrons)
$\text{Zn}^{2+}$ (Z = 30): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10}$ (0 unpaired electrons)
$\text{Ti}^{4+}$ (Z = 22): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$ (0 unpaired electrons)

Since $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ has a partially filled d-subshell, it will undergo d-d transitions and impart colour to the aqueous solution. The other ions have either empty or completely filled d-subshells and are colourless.

Answer: $\text{Cr}^{3+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The basic character of transition metal monoxides follows the order:
questions.solution:
For transition metal oxides in the same oxidation state, the basic character decreases as we move from left to right across a period.

This occurs because the effective nuclear charge increases and the ionic radius of the metal ion decreases ($Ti^{2+} \gt V^{2+} \gt Cr^{2+} \gt Fe^{2+}$). The decrease in size increases the polarizing power of the cation, leading to an increase in the covalent character of the metal-oxygen bond and a corresponding decrease in the basic character.

The atomic numbers of the given metals are $Ti$ ($22$), $V$ ($23$), $Cr$ ($24$), and $Fe$ ($26$).

Therefore, the correct order of basic character is $TiO \gt VO \gt CrO \gt FeO$.

Answer: $TiO \gt VO \gt CrO \gt FeO$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ on heating with aqueous NaOH gives -------------------------
questions.solution:
When potassium dichromate ($\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$) is treated with an alkali like aqueous NaOH, the orange dichromate ion is converted to the yellow chromate ion.

The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:
$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow 2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, the product formed is $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$.

Answer: $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The statements given below contain an assertion and reason. Choose the correct option. Assertion (A): Cr, Mo and W possess very high melting points in their respective series of elements. Reason (R): Cr, Mo and W have a large number of unpaired electrons, resulting in strong metallic bonding.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
questions.solution:
The melting points of transition metals depend on the strength of their metallic bonds.

The strength of metallic bonding is directly proportional to the number of unpaired electrons in the $(n-1)d$ and $ns$ subshells that can participate in the bonding.

Group 6 elements, Chromium (Cr), Molybdenum (Mo), and Tungsten (W), have a maximum or near-maximum number of unpaired electrons in their respective transition series. For example, Cr has the electronic configuration $[Ar] 3d^{5} 4s^{1}$, yielding six unpaired electrons.

This large number of unpaired electrons results in exceptionally strong interatomic metallic bonding.

Due to these strong metallic bonds, a large amount of thermal energy is required to separate the atoms, leading to very high melting points for Cr, Mo, and W in their respective series.

Thus, both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason is the correct explanation for the assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $3.482 \times 10^{-1}$g of Fe gets deposited when an aqueous solution of Ferric sulphate is electrolysed for 20 minutes using a current of "x" amperes. Find "x". (Atomic mass of Fe = 56amu).
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of ferric sulphate is $\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$. The reduction reaction at the cathode is:

$\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Fe}$

The number of electrons involved in the reduction of one $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion is $3$. Thus, the equivalent mass of iron is $E = \dfrac{56}{3}$.

According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis:

$W = \dfrac{E \cdot I \cdot t}{96500}$

Given:
Mass deposited, $W = 3.482 \times 10^{-1} \text{ g} = 0.3482 \text{ g}$
Time, $t = 20 \text{ minutes} = 20 \times 60 = 1200 \text{ s}$
Current, $I = x$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$0.3482 = \dfrac{56 \cdot x \cdot 1200}{3 \cdot 96500}$

$0.3482 = \dfrac{67200 \cdot x}{289500}$

$x = \dfrac{0.3482 \cdot 289500}{67200}$

$x = \dfrac{100803.9}{67200} = 1.5 \text{ A}$

Answer: $1.5\text{A}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider a Galvanic cell in which the following reactions occurs: $\text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Ag}^+(aq) \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}(aq) + \text{Ag}(s)$. What is the standard potential of the cell? Given: $E^0_{(\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag})} = aV$, $E^0_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = bV$ & $E^0_{(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe})} = cV$
questions.solution:
The given cell reaction is $\text{Fe}^{2+}(aq) + \text{Ag}^+(aq) \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+}(aq) + \text{Ag}(s)$.

The standard cell potential is given by:
$E^0_{\text{cell}} = E^0_{\text{cathode}} - E^0_{\text{anode}} = E^0_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}} - E^0_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}$

We are given:
$E^0_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}} = a$
$E^0_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}} = b$
$E^0_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}} = c$

To find $E^0_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}$, we use the relation $\Delta G^0 = -nFE^0$.
For the half-reaction $\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow \text{Fe}$, $\Delta G^0_1 = -3Fc$
For the half-reaction $\text{Fe}^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Fe}$, $\Delta G^0_2 = -2Fb$

The desired half-reaction is obtained by subtracting the second reaction from the first:
$\text{Fe}^{3+} + e^- \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}$

The standard free energy change for this reaction is:
$\Delta G^0_3 = \Delta G^0_1 - \Delta G^0_2$
$-1 \times F \times E^0_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}} = -3Fc - (-2Fb)$
$-F E^0_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}} = -3Fc + 2Fb$
$E^0_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}} = 3c - 2b$

Substituting this back into the equation for the standard cell potential:
$E^0_{\text{cell}} = a - (3c - 2b)$
$E^0_{\text{cell}} = a + 2b - 3c$

Answer: $(a + 2b - 3c)\,V$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What will be the change in the electrode potential of chromium electrode dipping into chromic sulphate solution, when the electrolyte is diluted 10 times at $25^\circ$C? [ $E^0\ (\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr})] = -0.74$V
questions.solution:
The reduction half-reaction for the chromium electrode is:

$\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow \text{Cr}$

The Nernst equation for the reduction potential is given by:

$E = E^0 - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{1}{[\text{Cr}^{3+}]}$

$E = E^0 + \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log [\text{Cr}^{3+}]$

Let the initial concentration of $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ be $c$. The initial electrode potential is:

$E_1 = E^0 + \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log c$

When the solution is diluted 10 times, the new concentration becomes $\dfrac{c}{10}$. The new electrode potential is:

$E_2 = E^0 + \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log \left(\dfrac{c}{10}\right)$

The change in electrode potential is:

$\Delta E = E_2 - E_1 = \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \left[ \log \left(\dfrac{c}{10}\right) - \log c \right]$

$\Delta E = \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \log \left(\dfrac{1}{10}\right)$

$\Delta E = \dfrac{0.0591}{3} \times (-1) = -0.0197 \text{ V}$

$\Delta E = -19.7 \text{ mV}$

The negative sign indicates that the electrode potential decreases by $19.7 \text{ mV}$.

Answer: Decrease by 19.7 mV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct mathematical expression which represents the variation in molar conductivity of a weak acid having concentration C and ionisation constant $K_a$
($\lambda_m^\infty$ = molar conductivity at infinite dilution, $\lambda_m$ = molar conductivity at concentration C)
questions.solution:
The degree of dissociation $\alpha$ for a weak electrolyte is given by:

$\alpha = \dfrac{\lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty}$

For a weak acid, the ionisation constant $K_a$ is given by Ostwald's dilution law:

$K_a = \dfrac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$

Substituting the expression for $\alpha$ into the equation for $K_a$:

$K_a = \dfrac{C \left( \dfrac{\lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty} \right)^2}{1 - \dfrac{\lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty}}$

$K_a = \dfrac{C \dfrac{\lambda_m^2}{(\lambda_m^\infty)^2}}{\dfrac{\lambda_m^\infty - \lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty}}$

$K_a = \dfrac{C \lambda_m^2}{\lambda_m^\infty (\lambda_m^\infty - \lambda_m)}$

Answer: $K_a = \lambda_m^2 C / \lambda_m^\infty(\lambda_m^\infty - \lambda_m)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, one Assertion and the other Reason are given. Choose the right option.
Assertion: The Molar conductivity of KCl increases very slowly with dilution and approaches a limiting value when dilution is infinite.
Reason: In case of KCl there is an increase in the number of ions on dilution due to complete ionisation at infinite dilution.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct
questions.solution:
KCl is a strong electrolyte and is completely ionised in solution at all concentrations. Therefore, the number of ions does not increase upon dilution.

The molar conductivity of a strong electrolyte like KCl increases slowly with dilution and approaches a limiting value at infinite dilution ($\Lambda_m^{\circ}$). This increase is not due to an increase in the number of ions, but rather due to a decrease in interionic attractions, which increases the mobility of the ions.

Thus, the Assertion is correct, but the Reason is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the mixtures listed in Column I with the correct method used for their separation.
Column IColumn II
A. Glycerol from spent LyeP. Steam distillation
B. Mixture of Benzoic acid and Naphthalene dissolved in organic solventQ. Distillation
C. Aniline & ChloroformR. Distillation under reduced pressure
D. 2- Nitrophenol & 4- NitrophenolS. Differential extraction using $\text{NaHCO}_3$
questions.solution:
Glycerol from spent lye is separated by distillation under reduced pressure because glycerol decomposes at its normal boiling point.

A mixture of benzoic acid and naphthalene dissolved in an organic solvent can be separated by differential extraction using aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$. Benzoic acid reacts with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ to form a water-soluble salt, while naphthalene remains in the organic layer.

Aniline (boiling point $457 \text{ K}$) and chloroform (boiling point $334 \text{ K}$) have a large difference in their boiling points and can be separated by simple distillation.

2-Nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol are separated by steam distillation. 2-Nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas 4-nitrophenol is not steam volatile due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

Thus, the correct matching is A \rightarrow R, B \rightarrow S, C \rightarrow Q, D \rightarrow P.

Answer: A — R B—S C—Q D—P

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is not the correct IUPAC name of the compound?
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate the IUPAC name for each given structure:

Option (A): The structure is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. The alkyl group attached to the oxygen atom is a 3-methylbutyl group. Thus, the ether is named 3-methylbutoxybenzene. This name is correct.

Option (B): The structure is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. The principal functional group is $-\text{OH}$, so the longest chain containing the $-\text{OH}$ group and the double bond is selected and numbered from the right to give the $-\text{OH}$ group the lowest locant (1). The substituents are a bromo group at C-2 and a methyl group at C-3. The name is 2-bromo-3-methylbut-2-en-1-ol. This name is correct.

Option (C): The structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3$. The principal chain must contain both $-\text{OH}$ groups. The longest such chain has 6 carbon atoms. Numbering from right to left gives the $-\text{OH}$ groups the lower locants (1,3) compared to left to right (4,6). The methyl substituents are at C-2 and C-5. The name is 2,5-dimethylhexane-1,3-diol. This name is correct.

Option (D): The structure is a cyclohexane ring with a propoxy group ($-\text{OC}_3\text{H}_7$) and two methyl groups on adjacent carbons. We must number the ring to give the lowest possible locant set for the substituents. Numbering from the carbon with the two methyl groups gives the locant set $1, 1, 2$. Numbering from the carbon with the propoxy group gives the locant set $1, 2, 2$. Comparing the two sets, $1, 1, 2$ is lower than $1, 2, 2$. Therefore, the methyl groups are at position 1 and the propoxy group is at position 2. Alphabetically, 'methyl' comes before 'propoxy'. The correct IUPAC name is 1,1-dimethyl-2-propoxycyclohexane. The given name 2,2-dimethyl-1-propoxycyclohexane is incorrect.

Answer: 2,2–Dimethyl–1–propoxycyclohexane:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Lassaigne's test for the detection of nitrogen fails in
questions.solution:
ion of the organic compound with sodium metal to form sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$).

For the formation of cyanide ion ($\text{CN}^{-}$), both carbon and nitrogen must be present in the organic compound.

Hydrazine hydrochloride ($\text{NH}_2\text{-NH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}$) does not contain carbon. Therefore, it cannot form sodium cyanide upon fusion with sodium metal, and Lassaigne's test for nitrogen fails.

The other compounds ($\text{NH}_2\text{CONH}_2$, $\text{NH}_2\text{CONHNH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}$, and $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NHNH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}$) contain both carbon and nitrogen, so they will give a positive test.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2\text{- NH}_2\text{HCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the compounds A and B from the following reaction sequence:
questions.solution:
The final products of reductive ozonolysis of compound B are acetaldehyde ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$) and 2-butanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$).

To find the structure of alkene B, we join the carbonyl carbons of the products with a double bond:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{O} + \text{O}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{reconstruct}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$
Thus, B is 3-methylpent-2-ene.

Compound A undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH to give B as the major product. According to Saytzeff's rule, the major product is the most substituted alkene.

Now check the given options for A:
In option (B), A is 3-bromo-3-methylpentane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(Br)}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).
Dehydrohalogenation of 3-bromo-3-methylpentane yields two possible alkenes:
1. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (3-methylpent-2-ene) - more substituted, major product.
2. $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)_2$ (2-ethylbut-1-ene) - less substituted, minor product.

Since the major product matches the structure of B, option (B) correctly identifies both A and B.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the wrong statement from the following
options: The product formed when (–)–2–Methylbutan–1–ol is heated with Conc. HCl is (+)–1–Chloro–2–methylbutane with Retention of configuration
Vinyl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reaction easily
$S_N1$ reaction of Alkyl halides is favoured by the presence of bulky substituents, protic solvents and the reaction products are a racemic mixture
$S_N2$ reaction of optically active halides are accompanied by Retention of configuration
questions.solution:
Option (A): The reaction of (–)–2–methylbutan–1–ol with conc. HCl involves the cleavage of the C–O bond at C1. The bonds attached to the chiral center at C2 are not broken, so the spatial arrangement (configuration) is retained. This statement is correct.

Option (B): Vinyl halides are highly unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution because the C–X bond acquires partial double bond character due to resonance, and the $sp^2$ hybridized carbon is less susceptible to nucleophilic attack. This statement is correct.

Option (C): $S_N1$ reactions are favored by bulky alkyl groups (which stabilize the carbocation and sterically hinder $S_N2$) and polar protic solvents. The carbocation intermediate is planar, allowing nucleophilic attack from both sides, which results in a racemic mixture. This statement is correct.

Option (D): $S_N2$ reactions of optically active halides proceed via a backside attack by the nucleophile. This leads to the inversion of configuration (Walden inversion), not retention. This statement is incorrect.

Answer: $S_N2$ reaction of optically active halides are accompanied by Retention of configuration

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Two statements, Assertion and Reason are given. With reference to them, choose the correct option.
Assertion: Hydrolysis of 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane follows $S_N1$ mechanism which involves 2 steps and the first step is:
The energy required to cleave C – Br is taken from the energy released due to Inductive effect and hyper-conjugative effect.
options: Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Reason is correct but Assertion is wrong
questions.solution:
The hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (a tertiary alkyl halide) proceeds via the $S_N1$ mechanism.

The $S_N1$ mechanism is a two-step process. The first step is the slow, reversible cleavage of the C-Br bond to form a stable tertiary carbocation and a bromide ion. Thus, the Assertion is correct.

The energy required to break the C-Br bond is obtained from the solvation of the resulting ions (carbocation and halide ion) by the polar protic solvent. While inductive and hyperconjugative effects stabilize the intermediate carbocation, they do not provide the energy for the initial bond cleavage. Thus, the Reason is incorrect.

Therefore, the Assertion is correct but the Reason is wrong.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is wrong

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Select the reagents needed to convert Benzene to 4–Bromophenylpropene in the correct sequential order.
(A). $\text{Cl}_2/\Delta$
(B). $(\text{CH}_3)_2$-CHCl /anhyd. $\text{AlCl}_3$
(C). Alc. KOH
(D). $\text{Br}_2$ / Fe
questions.solution:
The conversion of benzene to 4-bromophenylpropene involves the following sequential steps:

1. Friedel-Crafts Alkylation (Reagent B): Benzene reacts with isopropyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form isopropylbenzene (cumene).
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

2. Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (Reagent D): Isopropylbenzene undergoes bromination with $\text{Br}_2/\text{Fe}$. The isopropyl group is ortho/para-directing. Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product is 4-bromoisopropylbenzene.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Br}_2/\text{Fe} \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

3. Free Radical Halogenation (Reagent A): Treatment with $\text{Cl}_2/\Delta$ leads to substitution at the benzylic position, replacing the tertiary benzylic hydrogen with a chlorine atom to form 1-bromo-4-(2-chloropropan-2-yl)benzene.
$4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Cl}_2/\Delta \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

4. Dehydrohalogenation (Reagent C): Finally, reaction with alcoholic KOH causes E2 elimination of $\text{HCl}$, forming a double bond to yield 2-(4-bromophenyl)propene (a 4-bromophenylpropene derivative).
$4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Alc. KOH} \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$

The correct sequential order of reagents is B, D, A, C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitutions is:
questions.solution:
Reactivity towards electrophilic aromatic substitution depends on the electron density of the benzene ring. Electron-donating groups (EDG) increase the electron density and activate the ring, while electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) decrease the electron density and deactivate the ring.

Let us analyze the given compounds:
1. Compound (III) has an $-\text{OCH}_3$ group. It is a strongly activating group due to its strong $+R$ (resonance) effect, which outweighs its $-I$ effect.
2. Compound (I) has a $-\text{CH}_3$ group. It is an activating group due to its $+I$ (inductive) and $+H$ (hyperconjugation) effects. The $+R$ effect of $-\text{OCH}_3$ is stronger than the $+H$ effect of $-\text{CH}_3$, making compound (III) more reactive than compound (I).
3. Compound (II) is benzene, which has no substituents and serves as the reference.
4. Compound (IV) has a $-\text{CF}_3$ group. It is a strongly deactivating group due to its strong $-I$ effect.

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity towards electrophilic substitution is III $ \gt $ I $ \gt $ II $ \gt $ IV.

Answer: $III \gt I \gt II \gt IV$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound with molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$ that gives acetone on ozonolysis is:
questions.solution:
Ozonolysis of an alkene cleaves the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond to form carbonyl compounds.

Since one of the products is acetone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, the original alkene must contain a $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=$ group.

The molecular formula of the compound is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$. Subtracting the 3 carbon atoms of the acetone fragment leaves 2 carbon atoms for the other fragment, which must be an ethylidene group, $=\text{CHCH}_3$.

Combining these two fragments, the structure of the alkene is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3$, which is 2-methyl-2-butene.

The ozonolysis reaction is:
$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{O}_3, \text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{O} + \text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$

Answer: 2-methyl-2-butene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 2-butyne is treated with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4/\text{HgSO}_4$, the product formed is:
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkyne with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the presence of $\text{HgSO}_4$ is known as Kucherov's reaction, which results in the hydration of the alkyne.

For 2-butyne ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3$), the addition of a water molecule across the triple bond initially forms an unstable enol intermediate.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+}, \text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$

The enol intermediate undergoes tautomerization to form the more stable keto form, which is butanone.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OH})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$

Thus, the final product is butanone.

Answer: Butanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is NOT in accordance with the property stated against it?
options: $HI  \gt  HBr  \gt  HCl  \gt  HF$ [Acidic Property in Water]
questions.solution:
The oxidising power of halogens decreases down the group: $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$.

The acidic strength of hydrogen halides in water increases down the group due to a decrease in bond dissociation enthalpy: $HI \gt HBr \gt HCl \gt HF$.

Electronegativity decreases down the group: $F \gt Cl \gt Br \gt I$.

The bond dissociation energy of halogens does not follow a regular trend. Due to strong interelectronic repulsions between the lone pairs on the small fluorine atoms, the $F-F$ bond is weaker than the $Cl-Cl$ and $Br-Br$ bonds. The correct order of bond dissociation energy is $Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt F_2 \gt I_2$.

Thus, the order $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$ for bond dissociation energy is incorrect.

Answer: $F_2 \gt Cl_2 \gt Br_2 \gt I_2$ [Bond Dissociation Energy]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In the reaction,
$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{CrO}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
The change in oxidation state of Cr is:
questions.solution:
In $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Cr is calculated as:

$2x + 7(-2) = -2$

$2x = +12 \Rightarrow x = +6$

In $\text{CrO}_5$, the molecule has a butterfly structure containing two peroxo linkages ($-O-O-$) and one oxo linkage ($=O$).

There are four oxygen atoms with an oxidation state of $-1$ and one oxygen atom with an oxidation state of $-2$.

The oxidation state of Cr in $\text{CrO}_5$ is calculated as:

$y + 4(-1) + 1(-2) = 0$

$y = +6$

Thus, the oxidation state of Cr remains $+6$ in both the reactant and the product. There is no change in the oxidation state of Cr.

Answer: No change in oxidation state

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 0.02M solution of sucrose is isotonic with 0.008M solution of sodium sulphate. What is the percentage dissociation of the electrolyte?
questions.solution:
For isotonic solutions, the osmotic pressures are equal.

$\pi_{sucrose} = \pi_{Na_2SO_4}$

$i_1 C_1 RT = i_2 C_2 RT$

For sucrose (a non-electrolyte), $i_1 = 1$.

$1 \times 0.02 = i_2 \times 0.008$

$i_2 = \dfrac{0.02}{0.008} = 2.5$

Sodium sulphate ($Na_2SO_4$) dissociates into $3$ ions ($2Na^+$ and $SO_4^{2-}$), so $n = 3$.

The van't Hoff factor is given by $i = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha$.

$2.5 = 1 + (3 - 1)\alpha$

$2.5 = 1 + 2\alpha$

$2\alpha = 1.5$

$\alpha = 0.75$

Percentage dissociation = $0.75 \times 100 = 75\%$.

Answer: $75$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage dissociation of 0.8ml of Acetic acid (density is 1.04g/ml) which is dissolved in 1.2L of water if the observed Depression in freezing point is 0.0228 K? ($K_f$ for water = 1.86Kkg/mol.)
questions.solution:
Mass of acetic acid $= \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 0.8 \times 1.04 = 0.832 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) $= 60 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of acetic acid $= \dfrac{0.832}{60} = 0.01387 \text{ mol}$

Mass of water $= 1.2 \text{ L} \times 1 \text{ kg/L} = 1.2 \text{ kg}$

Molality ($m$) $= \dfrac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}} = \dfrac{0.01387}{1.2} = 0.01156 \text{ mol/kg}$

Theoretical depression in freezing point ($\Delta T_{f(\text{th})}$) $= K_f \times m = 1.86 \times 0.01156 = 0.0215 \text{ K}$

Observed depression in freezing point ($\Delta T_f$) $= 0.0228 \text{ K}$

van't Hoff factor ($i$) $= \dfrac{\text{Observed } \Delta T_f}{\text{Theoretical } \Delta T_{f(\text{th})}} = \dfrac{0.0228}{0.0215} \approx 1.06$

For the dissociation of acetic acid:
$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+$

$i = 1 + \alpha$

$1.06 = 1 + \alpha \Rightarrow \alpha = 0.06$

Percentage dissociation $= \alpha \times 100 = 0.06 \times 100 = 6\%$

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement
options: At the freezing point of a solution containing a non-volatile solute, the vapour pressure of the liquid solvent becomes less than that of the solid solvent
A hypotonic solution is more concentrated with respect to the other solution separated from it by a semi permeable membrane
In case of dissociation of solute particles in a solution, the van't Hoff factor is more than unity because the observed molar mass has a lesser value
The molal boiling point elevation constant for a solvent is directly proportional to its enthalpy of vaporisation
questions.solution:
At the freezing point of a solution, the vapour pressure of the liquid solvent in the solution is equal to the vapour pressure of the pure solid solvent. Thus, statement (A) is incorrect.

A hypotonic solution has a lower osmotic pressure and is less concentrated compared to the other solution. Thus, statement (B) is incorrect.

In the case of dissociation of solute particles, the number of particles in the solution increases. The van't Hoff factor $i$ is greater than $1$. Since $i = \dfrac{\text{Normal molar mass}}{\text{Observed molar mass}}$, an $i \gt 1$ implies that the observed molar mass is less than the normal molar mass. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

The molal boiling point elevation constant is given by $K_b = \dfrac{R T_b^2 M}{1000 \Delta_{vap}H}$. It is inversely proportional to the enthalpy of vaporisation $\Delta_{vap}H$. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

Answer: In case of dissociation of solute particles in a solution, the van't Hoff factor is more than unity because the observed molar mass has a lesser value

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An aqueous solution of an unknown solute "X" is prepared by adding 4.0g of it into 2.0moles of water. What is the mass percent of "X" in the aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
Mass of solute $X = 4.0$ g

Moles of water $= 2.0$ mol

Molar mass of water $= 18$ g/mol

Mass of water $= 2.0 \times 18 = 36.0$ g

Total mass of solution $= 4.0 + 36.0 = 40.0$ g

Mass percent of $X = \left( \dfrac{4.0}{40.0} \right) \times 100 = 10$

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The mass of precipitate formed when 50 mL of 16.9% aqueous solution of $\text{AgNO}_3$ is mixed with 50 mL of 5.8% NaCl solution is------------g
[Ag = 107.8, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, Cl = 35.5]
questions.solution:
Mass of $\text{AgNO}_3$ in 50 mL of 16.9% solution = $\dfrac{16.9}{100} \times 50 = 8.45$ g

Molar mass of $\text{AgNO}_3$ = $107.8 + 14 + 3 \times 16 = 169.8$ g/mol

Moles of $\text{AgNO}_3$ = $\dfrac{8.45}{169.8} \approx 0.0497$ mol

Mass of NaCl in 50 mL of 5.8% solution = $\dfrac{5.8}{100} \times 50 = 2.9$ g

Molar mass of NaCl = $23 + 35.5 = 58.5$ g/mol

Moles of NaCl = $\dfrac{2.9}{58.5} \approx 0.0495$ mol

The balanced chemical equation is:

$\text{AgNO}_3 + \text{NaCl} \rightarrow \text{AgCl} + \text{NaNO}_3$

Since 1 mole of $\text{AgNO}_3$ reacts with 1 mole of NaCl, NaCl is the limiting reagent.

Moles of AgCl precipitate formed = $0.0495$ mol

Molar mass of AgCl = $107.8 + 35.5 = 143.3$ g/mol

Mass of AgCl formed = $0.0495 \times 143.3 \approx 7.1$ g

The closest integer value is 7 g.

Answer: $7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the molar masses of two chemically non-reacting gases $\text{A}_2$ and $\text{B}_2$ are 28 amu and 32 amu respectively and 0.8g of $\text{A}_2$ and 0.4g of $\text{B}_2$ are enclosed in a container with a total pressure of 820 mm of Hg, then the partial pressure of $\text{A}_2$ in atmosphere unit is ----------
questions.solution:
Number of moles of $\text{A}_2$, $n_{\text{A}_2} = \dfrac{0.8}{28} = \dfrac{1}{35}$

Number of moles of $\text{B}_2$, $n_{\text{B}_2} = \dfrac{0.4}{32} = \dfrac{1}{80}$

Total number of moles, $n_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{1}{35} + \dfrac{1}{80} = \dfrac{16 + 7}{560} = \dfrac{23}{560}$

Mole fraction of $\text{A}_2$, $x_{\text{A}_2} = \dfrac{n_{\text{A}_2}}{n_{\text{total}}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{35}}{\dfrac{23}{560}} = \dfrac{16}{23}$

Total pressure, $P_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{820}{760} \text{ atm} = \dfrac{41}{38} \text{ atm}$

Partial pressure of $\text{A}_2$, $P_{\text{A}_2} = x_{\text{A}_2} \times P_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{16}{23} \times \dfrac{41}{38} = \dfrac{328}{437} \approx 0.75 \text{ atm}$

Answer: $0.75$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom (n=1) is 0.530 Å. The radius of the first excited state orbit in Å is:
questions.solution:
The radius of the $n$th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by $r_n = r_1 \times \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$.

For a hydrogen atom, $Z = 1$.

The first excited state corresponds to $n = 2$.

Given $r_1 = 0.530$ Å.

Substituting the values, we get $r_2 = 0.530 \times \dfrac{2^2}{1} = 0.530 \times 4 = 2.12$ Å.

Answer: $2.12$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the photoelectric emission, the energy of the emitted electron is:
options: greater than the energy of the incident photon
proportional to the intensity of the incident photon
same as that of the incident photon
smaller than the energy of the incident photon
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electron is given by:

$K_{\max} = E - \Phi$

where $E$ is the energy of the incident photon and $\Phi$ is the work function of the material.

Since the work function $\Phi$ is always positive for any material, the maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$ is strictly less than the energy of the incident photon $E$.

The actual kinetic energy of an emitted electron ranges from $0$ to $K_{\max}$.

Therefore, the energy of the emitted electron is always smaller than the energy of the incident photon.

Answer: smaller than the energy of the incident photon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Ozone is formed by the reaction
$\text{O}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{(g)} \rightarrow \text{O}_{3(g)},\ \Delta H = -107.2\ kJ$.
Given O=O bond energy is 498.0 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$, the average bond energy of ozone is:
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of the reaction is given by the difference between the sum of bond energies of reactants and products.

$\Delta H = \sum \text{BE(reactants)} - \sum \text{BE(products)}$

For the given reaction $\text{O}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{(g)} \rightarrow \text{O}_{3(g)}$:

$\Delta H = \text{BE(O=O)} - 2 \times \text{BE(O-O in O}_3)$

Substituting the given values:

$-107.2 = 498.0 - 2 \times \text{BE(O-O in O}_3)$

$2 \times \text{BE(O-O in O}_3) = 498.0 + 107.2$

$2 \times \text{BE(O-O in O}_3) = 605.2$

$\text{BE(O-O in O}_3) = \dfrac{605.2}{2} = 302.6\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $302.6\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ for a reaction are 35.5 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ and 83.6 J $\text{K}^{-1}$ respectively. Assuming that $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ do not vary with temperature, the reaction is spontaneous when:
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, $\Delta G \lt 0$.

Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

For spontaneity:

$\Delta H - T\Delta S \lt 0$

$T \gt \dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$

Given values are:

$\Delta H = 35.5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 35500 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta S = 83.6 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values:

$T \gt \dfrac{35500}{83.6}$

$T \gt 424.64 \text{ K}$

Therefore, the reaction is spontaneous when $T \gt 425 \text{ K}$.

Answer: $T \gt 425\ K$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The heat of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is -393.5 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$.
The heat released on the formation of 35.2 g of $\text{CO}_2$ by combustion of C is:
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction of carbon is given by:

$\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} \quad \Delta H = -393.5\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Molar mass of $\text{CO}_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of $\text{CO}_2$ formed $= \dfrac{35.2}{44} = 0.8\ \text{mol}$

Enthalpy change for the formation of $0.8\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}_2 = 0.8 \times (-393.5\ \text{kJ}) = -314.8\ \text{kJ}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the heat released (enthalpy change) is approximately $-315\ \text{kJ}$.

Answer: $-315\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A square plate is contracting at a uniform rate of 2 $\text{cm}^2$ / min. The rate at which the perimeter is decreasing when the side of the square is 16 cm is:
questions.solution:
Let $x$ be the side length of the square plate.

Area of the square, $A = x^2$

Perimeter of the square, $P = 4x$

Given that the area is contracting at a uniform rate of $2\ \text{cm}^2/\text{min}$, we have:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -2$

Differentiating $A = x^2$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2x \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

Substituting $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = -2$ and $x = 16$:

$-2 = 2(16) \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{16}\ \text{cm}/\text{min}$

Now, differentiating $P = 4x$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 4 \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$:

$\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 4 \left(-\dfrac{1}{16}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{4}\ \text{cm}/\text{min}$

The negative sign indicates that the perimeter is decreasing. Therefore, the rate at which the perimeter is decreasing is $\dfrac{1}{4}\ \text{cm}/\text{min}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4}\ cm\ /\ min$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If 3 cm/s is the rate at which the side of an equilateral triangle increases, then the rate of change of area, when the side is 12 cm is:
questions.solution:
Let the side of the equilateral triangle be $a$ and its area be $A$.

The area of an equilateral triangle is given by $A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^2$.

Differentiating with respect to time $t$, we get:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 2a \times \dfrac{da}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} a \dfrac{da}{dt}$

Given that $\dfrac{da}{dt} = 3 \text{ cm/s}$ and $a = 12 \text{ cm}$, substituting these values:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12 \times 3 = 18\sqrt{3} \text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$

Answer: $18\sqrt{3} \ \text{cm}^2 / \text{s}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The behaviour of the function $f(x) = \sin\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ on $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8} , \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \sin\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 2\cos\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

For the given interval $x \in \left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}, \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$:

$\dfrac{3\pi}{4} \lt 2x \lt \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$

$\dfrac{3\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{4} \lt 2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} \lt \dfrac{5\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$\pi \lt 2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4} \lt \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$

In the interval $\left(\pi, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, the cosine function is negative.

Therefore, $\cos\left(2x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) \lt 0 \Rightarrow f'(x) \lt 0$

Hence, $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing on $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8}, \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$.

Answer: Strictly decreasing on $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{8} , \dfrac{5\pi}{8}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x) = x^4 - 31x^2 + ax + 5$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, then the value of '$a$' is ___ and the function attains a ___ at $x = 1$
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = x^4 - 31x^2 + ax + 5$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = 4x^3 - 62x + a$

Since $f(x)$ has a turning point at $x = 1$, $f'(1) = 0$

$4(1)^3 - 62(1) + a = 0$

$a = 58$

Now, finding the second derivative:

$f''(x) = 12x^2 - 62$

At $x = 1$, $f''(1) = 12(1)^2 - 62 = -50$

Since $f''(1) \lt 0$, the function attains a local maxima at $x = 1$.

Answer: $a = 58$ , local maxima

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region bounded by the line $y = x + 2$ and the curve $x = -y^2$ is
questions.solution:
The given curves are $x = -y^2$ and $y = x + 2$.

To find the points of intersection, substitute $x = y - 2$ into the equation of the parabola:

$y - 2 = -y^2$

$y^2 + y - 2 = 0$

$(y + 2)(y - 1) = 0$

The points of intersection are at $y = -2$ and $y = 1$.

The area of the bounded region is given by integrating the difference of the right curve $x = -y^2$ and the left curve $x = y - 2$ with respect to $y$ from $y = -2$ to $y = 1$:

$A = \int_{-2}^{1} (-y^2 - (y - 2)) \, dy$

$A = \int_{-2}^{1} (-y^2 - y + 2) \, dy$

Integrating the expression:

$A = \left[ -\dfrac{y^3}{3} - \dfrac{y^2}{2} + 2y \right]_{-2}^{1}$

Substituting the upper limit $y = 1$:

$-\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2} + 2 = \dfrac{-2 - 3 + 12}{6} = \dfrac{7}{6}$

Substituting the lower limit $y = -2$:

$-\dfrac{(-2)^3}{3} - \dfrac{(-2)^2}{2} + 2(-2) = \dfrac{8}{3} - 2 - 4 = -\dfrac{10}{3}$

Calculating the total area:

$A = \dfrac{7}{6} - \left( -\dfrac{10}{3} \right) = \dfrac{7}{6} + \dfrac{20}{6} = \dfrac{27}{6} = 4.5$

Answer: $4.5\ \text{sq units}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed by the $x$-axis, the line $x = \sqrt{3}\,y$ and the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$ is
questions.solution:
The given circle is $x^2 + y^2 = 4$, which has its center at the origin $(0,0)$ and radius $r = 2$.

The given line is $x = \sqrt{3}y$, which can be rewritten as $y = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}x$.

The angle made by this line with the positive $x$-axis is $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

The required region in the first quadrant is a sector of the circle bounded by the $x$-axis ($\theta = 0$) and the line ($\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$).

The area of a circular sector is given by $\dfrac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$.

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times (2)^2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ sq units.

Alternatively, using integration by finding the intersection point $(\sqrt{3}, 1)$:

Area $= \int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}} dx + \int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} \sqrt{4 - x^2} dx$

Area $= \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2\sqrt{3}} \right]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} + \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{4-x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \right]_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}$

Area $= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \left( \pi - \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} \right) \right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ sq units.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\ sq\ units$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: "A storage room must be kept at a temperature (T) such that triple the temperature is at least 15° C, but the temperature plus 8 is not more than 20° C. What is the range of safe temperatures?"
questions.solution:
From the given problem, the temperature $T$ must satisfy two conditions.

The first condition is that triple the temperature is at least $15$. This can be written as the inequality:

$3T \ge 15$

Dividing both sides by $3$ yields:

$T \ge 5$

The second condition is that the temperature plus $8$ is not more than $20$. This can be written as the inequality:

$T + 8 \le 20$

Subtracting $8$ from both sides yields:

$T \le 12$

Combining the two inequalities gives the range of safe temperatures:

$5 \le T \le 12$

In interval notation, this represents the closed interval $[5, 12]$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The remainder when $7^{103}$ is divided by $25$ is
questions.solution:
We need to find the remainder when $7^{103}$ is divided by $25$.

We can write $7^{103}$ as $7 \cdot 7^{102} = 7 \cdot (7^2)^{51}$.

We know that $7^2 = 49 \equiv -1 \pmod{25}$.

Raising both sides to the power of $51$, we get:

$(7^2)^{51} \equiv (-1)^{51} \pmod{25}$

$7^{102} \equiv -1 \pmod{25}$

Multiplying both sides by $7$, we get:

$7^{103} \equiv -7 \pmod{25}$

To find the positive remainder, we add $25$ to $-7$:

$-7 + 25 = 18$

Thus, the remainder when $7^{103}$ is divided by $25$ is $18$.

Answer: $18$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The radius of a circle is 5 cm. A chord of this circle is equal to the radius. Then the length of the arc of this chord is:
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the circle be $r = 5$ cm.

Since the length of the chord is equal to the radius, the triangle formed by the chord and the two radii connecting its endpoints to the center is an equilateral triangle.

Therefore, the angle subtended by the chord at the center is $\theta = 60^\circ = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ radians.

The length of the arc is given by the formula $l = r\theta$.

$l = 5 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$l = \dfrac{5 \times 3.1416}{3} \approx 5.236$ cm

Rounding to two decimal places, the length of the arc is $5.24$ cm.

Answer: $5.24 \ cm$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The conjugate of $z = \dfrac{(4 + i)(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(2 - i)}$
questions.solution:
$z = \dfrac{(4 + i)(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(2 - i)}$

Simplifying the numerator and denominator:

$(4 + i)(1 - i) = 4 - 4i + i - i^2 = 5 - 3i$

$(1 + i)(2 - i) = 2 - i + 2i - i^2 = 3 + i$

Substituting these values:

$z = \dfrac{5 - 3i}{3 + i}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$z = \dfrac{5 - 3i}{3 + i} \times \dfrac{3 - i}{3 - i}$

$z = \dfrac{15 - 5i - 9i + 3i^2}{3^2 - i^2}$

$z = \dfrac{15 - 14i - 3}{9 + 1}$

$z = \dfrac{12 - 14i}{10} = \dfrac{6}{5} - \dfrac{7}{5}i$

The conjugate of $z$ is:

$\bar{z} = \dfrac{6}{5} + \dfrac{7}{5}i$

Answer: $\dfrac{6}{5} + \dfrac{7}{5} i$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\sqrt{1+x} - \sqrt{1-x}}{\sin x}, & x \neq 0 \\ k, & x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then $k =$
questions.solution:
For the function to be continuous at $x = 0$, we must have $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = f(0) = k$.

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sqrt{1+x} - \sqrt{1-x}}{\sin x}$

Rationalizing the numerator:

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(\sqrt{1+x} - \sqrt{1-x})(\sqrt{1+x} + \sqrt{1-x})}{\sin x (\sqrt{1+x} + \sqrt{1-x})}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(1+x) - (1-x)}{\sin x (\sqrt{1+x} + \sqrt{1-x})}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2x}{\sin x (\sqrt{1+x} + \sqrt{1-x})}$

Using the standard limit $\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x}{\sin x} = 1$:

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1+x} + \sqrt{1-x}} \times \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x}{\sin x}$

$= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1+0} + \sqrt{1-0}} \times 1$

$= \dfrac{2}{2} = 1$

Therefore, $k = 1$.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The function $y = ||x| - 1|$ is differentiable for all values of '$x$' except
questions.solution:
The given function is $y = ||x| - 1|$.

A function of the form $|f(x)|$ is generally non-differentiable at points where $f(x) = 0$ (if the curve crosses the x-axis) and at points where $f(x)$ itself is non-differentiable.

First, the inner function $f(x) = |x| - 1$ involves $|x|$, which is non-differentiable at $x = 0$.
For $x$ in the neighborhood of $0$ (i.e., $-1 \lt x \lt 1$), $y = ||x| - 1| = 1 - |x|$.
The left-hand derivative at $x = 0$ is $1$ and the right-hand derivative is $-1$. Thus, $y$ is non-differentiable at $x = 0$.

Second, we check where the expression inside the outer modulus becomes zero:
$|x| - 1 = 0$
$\Rightarrow |x| = 1$
$\Rightarrow x = 1$ or $x = -1$

At $x = 1$, for $x \gt 1$, $y = x - 1$ (derivative is $1$). For $0 \lt x \lt 1$, $y = 1 - x$ (derivative is $-1$). Thus, $y$ is non-differentiable at $x = 1$.

At $x = -1$, for $x \lt -1$, $y = -x - 1$ (derivative is $-1$). For $-1 \lt x \lt 0$, $y = x + 1$ (derivative is $1$). Thus, $y$ is non-differentiable at $x = -1$.

Therefore, the function is differentiable for all values of $x$ except at $x \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$.

Answer: $\{-1 , 0 , 1\}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin^5 x \cos^7 x \ dx =$
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_{-\dfrac{\pi}{2}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} \sin^5 x \cos^7 x \ dx$

Let $f(x) = \sin^5 x \cos^7 x$

$f(-x) = \sin^5(-x) \cos^7(-x)$

$f(-x) = (-\sin x)^5 (\cos x)^7$

$f(-x) = -\sin^5 x \cos^7 x = -f(x)$

Since $f(x)$ is an odd function, the integral over the symmetric interval $[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}]$ is $0$.

$I = 0$

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Given $P = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & \alpha & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ is the adjoint of a $3 \times 3$ matrix A and $|A| = 3$, then the value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.solution:
Given $P = \text{adj}(A)$ and $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix.

We know that $|\text{adj}(A)| = |A|^{n-1}$, where $n$ is the order of the matrix.

Here, $n = 3$ and $|A| = 3$.

$|P| = |A|^{3-1} = |A|^2 = 3^2 = 9$

Now, calculating the determinant of matrix $P$:

$|P| = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & \alpha & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding along the first row:

$|P| = 2(2 \times 3 - 2 \times 3) - \alpha(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 1) + 1(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 1)$

$|P| = 2(0) - \alpha(1) + 1(1)$

$|P| = 1 - \alpha$

Equating the two values of $|P|$:

$1 - \alpha = 9$

$\alpha = -8$

Answer: $-8$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \dfrac{dx}{dy} = x$ is:
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \dfrac{dx}{dy} = x$.

We know that $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{dy}{dx}}$.

Substituting this in the given equation, we get:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{dy}{dx}} = x$

Multiplying both sides by $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, we get:

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 + 1 = x \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 - x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 1 = 0$

The highest order derivative present in the equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, so the order is $1$.

The highest power of the highest order derivative is $3$, so the degree is $3$.

Thus, the order and degree are $(1, 3)$.

Answer: $(1, 3)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The particular solution of the equation $\sin\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = a$, where $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y = 2$ when $x = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is $\sin\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = a$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sin^{-1}(a)$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\int dy = \int \sin^{-1}(a) dx$

$y = x \sin^{-1}(a) + C$

Substituting $y = 2$ when $x = 0$:

$2 = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = 2$

Substituting $C = 2$ in the general solution:

$y = x \sin^{-1}(a) + 2$

$\dfrac{y - 2}{x} = \sin^{-1}(a)$

$\sin\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x}\right) = a$

Answer: $\sin\left(\dfrac{y-2}{x}\right) = a$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a bank the principal increases continuously at the rate of 4% per annum. In how many years will ₹1000 triple itself?
questions.solution:
Let $P$ be the principal at any time $t$.

The rate of increase of principal is given by $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = \dfrac{4}{100}P$

$\dfrac{dP}{P} = 0.04 dt$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{dP}{P} = \int 0.04 dt$

$\log_e P = 0.04 t + C$

At $t = 0$, $P = 1000$, which gives $C = \log_e 1000$

Substituting $C$ back into the equation:

$\log_e P = 0.04 t + \log_e 1000$

$\log_e \left(\dfrac{P}{1000}\right) = 0.04 t$

To find the time when the principal triples, substitute $P = 3000$:

$\log_e \left(\dfrac{3000}{1000}\right) = 0.04 t$

$\log_e 3 = \dfrac{4}{100} t$

$t = 25 \log_e 3$

Answer: $25\log_e 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of $dy = \cos x (2 - y \ \text{cosec} \ x) dx$ where $y = \sqrt{2}$ when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is
questions.solution:
The given differential equation can be rewritten as:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\cos x - y \cos x \text{cosec} x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \cot x = 2\cos x$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P y = Q$, where $P = \cot x$ and $Q = 2\cos x$.

The integrating factor (IF) is:

$\text{IF} = e^{\int \cot x dx} = e^{\ln(\sin x)} = \sin x$
